video.title: The middle and the spread: Mean, median, mode and range
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Charts draw themselves; code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello - primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Narrator - the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: A parent asked me: how did the class do in the maths test? I had nine marks in front of me. I could not read all nine to every parent. I needed one fair number.
Today: three kinds of middle, and how to measure the spread.

scenes.on_screen_text: The mean: share it out equally
scenes.narration: The mean is what everyone would get if we shared the total equally. Add all the marks, then divide by how many there are. Our nine marks add to one hundred and sixteen, so the mean is about thirteen.
The median is the middle mark when you line them up in order. With nine marks, it is the fifth one. Here, the median is thirteen.
The mode is the mark that appears most often. Here, twelve and fourteen both appear twice, so there are two modes. The mode is handy for things you cannot add, like favourite colours.
Now watch. One pupil was ill and scored zero. The mean drops to about eleven. The median only moves to twelve. One extreme mark pulls the mean, but hardly moves the median.
A middle alone is not enough. Two classes can have the same mean, but one has marks from nine to sixteen, and the other from two to twenty. The range, highest minus lowest, shows the spread.
Quick check! Most pupils get a little pocket money, but one gets a lot. Which middle describes a typical pupil best?
The median. The one big amount pulls the mean up, so the mean looks richer than most pupils are. The median stays with the typical pupil.

scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: the middle and the spread
scenes.narration: In the app, open The middle and the spread. Drag one pupil's mark from zero to twenty, and watch the mean, median, mode and range react.

scenes.on_screen_text: What does the range tell us?
scenes.narration: Your turn. A class has a range of eighteen marks. What does that tell you about the class?
The marks are very spread out. Remember: the mean shares out, the median is the middle, the mode is the most common. And always give a spread with your middle.
Try it in class tomorrow: line up nine pupils by height. The fifth pupil is the median. Then work out the mean and the range together on the board.

checkpoints.prompt: Most pupils get a little pocket money, one gets a lot. Which middle describes a typical pupil?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: the median is not pulled by one very large amount.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: one large amount pulls the mean up. The median stays with the typical pupil.

checkpoints.prompt: A class has a range of 18 marks. What does that tell you?

options.text: The marks are very spread out

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: the highest and lowest marks are 18 apart, so the class is very mixed.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: the range is highest minus lowest. It measures spread, not the middle.
